source_meaning: Grammar exercise set (multiple choice): (1) I always choose and buy fruit that looks fresh (a. looks good); (2) if the weather is good, I go jogging (b. yokereba); (3) over there it says no photography, but people take pictures (b. written); (4) A: I spent all my money on the trip. What should I do? B: In that case, my friend's company is recruiting part-timers — shall I introduce you? (d. soko de); (5) I haven't told anyone this yet (d. haven't told). / Conjunctions (a. wari ni wa, b. beki da, c. koto wa nai, d. kara ni wa, e. sei de, f. ni kuwaete): (1) having spent this much money, I absolutely refuse to fail; (2) because he was seriously ill as a child, he is still weak; (3) despite spending time on practice, no good results came; (4) besides new words every day, I also study new grammar; (5) I told her everything I should say; (6) there are 30 minutes until the Shinkansen departs, so no need to hurry. / Particles (a. no ni, b. sei de, c. tara, d. ni taishite, e. kurai): (1) those with questions about the current presentation, please raise your hand; (2) after three days off in a row, the roads are very crowded today; (3) you can't tell what kind of person someone is after just a brief acquaintance; (4) Manager: You should have come to yesterday's meeting — I said important things. Employee: I'm sorry; (5) though I thought my talk was boring, I received applause. / (a. tokoro ni, b. ni taishite, c. you ni, d. tame ni, e. to itte mo): (1) my writing will appear in a magazine — though it's just a school magazine; (2) those with opinions on the current remark, please raise your hand; (3) just as the closing greeting ended, Nakamura walked in; (4) because neighbors often don't take out the trash late, I put up a poster; (5) to study design, I attend a vocational school. / (a. te, b. darake, c. shi, d. kara, e. ga, f. nante, g. made, h. no ni): (1) failed the exam again? That's because you don't study seriously; (2) although it is raining, the match has begun; (3) there's no need to discuss this anymore; (4) this apartment is far from the station and inconvenient; (5) not just stories — economics and history have also been made into manga; (6) late again? Even though you live close; (7) this car has good design and good performance, so I want to buy it; (8) I was too busy to clean for days, so the room is covered in dust. / (a. ni tsurete, b. to iu koto, c. ni kakete, d. ni oite, e. koto desu, f. ni yotte, g. naranai, h. darou, i. ni okeru): (1) it says "be quiet in the library" — you must not chat; (2) I think this illness will probably heal soon; (3) even for the same dish, the taste differs by restaurant; (4) in work, communication skills are very important; (5) from April to August I traveled all over the country; (6) after leaving the hospital, my strength recovered as days passed; (7) in my parents' generation, it was an era when you could earn a lot; (8) Publisher: I'd like to publish this book in early autumn. Author: So you want the manuscript by June, right? / Change expressions (a. you ni narimashita, b. kita, c. narimashita, d. kimashita, e. iku deshou): (1) I became a working adult this April. I used to sleep in, but now I can get up early. I've gotten used to work. From now on my work will gradually increase; (2) A: How's your Japanese study? B: I feel it's getting gradually harder. But I can understand anime and TV programs a little now. And for easy books, I use the dictionary less when reading. A: You've worked hard. You'll keep getting better. / Intention (a. tsumori da, b. tsumori desu, c. koto ni narimasu). / Te-forms (a. te aru, b. te oku, c. ga suru, d. te iru, e. o suru) — meeting prep dialogue: A: I made tomorrow's materials, please check. B: This is OK. Please make 13 copies. A: Got it. B: And have you bought the drinks yet? A: Yes, I've rearranged the chairs and tables, and decorated with flowers. B: Oh, pretty. What flower is that? It smells nice. A: Yes, those flowers are shaped like stars. I don't remember the name, but they smell good so I bought them. B: Hey, the window is open. Shall I close it? A: No, it's hot, so I've left it open. You don't have to close it. / (a. doori, b. omoidasareru, c. gachi, d. hazukashigatte iru, e. toori): (1) she blushes as soon as she appears in front of people; (2) I tried the experiment as written in the textbook, but it didn't go well; (3) hearing this song brings back memories of my student days; (4) if you perform at your practiced level, you'll surely win; (5) when I'm short on time before going out, I tend to carelessly forget things. / Indirect commands example: teacher ⇒ children (be quiet) → The teacher told the children "Be quiet." (1) PE teacher ⇒ students (move forward); (2) cooking class instructor ⇒ students (be careful with knives); (3) bus driver ⇒ passengers (sit in your seats). / Negative commands: teacher ⇒ children (don't speak loudly in the library) → "Don't speak loudly in the library." (1) IT teacher ⇒ students (don't tell others your password); (2) home economics teacher ⇒ students (be careful of burns when cooking); (3) parents ⇒ children (don't cry over small injuries). / Emotion verbs: the kids are too noisy / (teacher ⇒ children / be quiet) get angry → The teacher angrily said "Be quiet." (1) many cars, dangerous / (mother ⇒ child / watch out for cars) warn; (2) mealtime is near / (mother ⇒ child / don't just eat snacks, help prepare dinner) say; (3) the room is messy / (father ⇒ child / tidy up) scold. / Following instructions: the doctor said / take medicine → I take the medicine as the doctor said. (1) it's written in the recipe / make a cake; (2) the announcer's pronunciation / please pronounce accordingly; (3) the instruction manual / assemble the bookshelf. / Degree: I feel dizzy / I'm hungry → I'm so hungry I feel dizzy. (1) want to watch many times / it's a wonderful movie; (2) can use for decades / it's a sturdy chair; (3) can't sleep all night / I'm worried. / Emotion: the neighbor boy / scared of dogs → The neighbor boy is afraid of dogs. (1) Tanaka / wants kabuki tickets; (2) Nakamura / wants to study abroad; (3) Li / feels lonely. / Potential negative: such an expensive condo / no one can buy → No one can buy such an expensive condo. (1) that person's feelings / I can't understand; (2) literary matters / I don't understand; (3) this secret / can't tell even close friends. / Opinion: independent learning is important / very important → A: Is independent learning important? B: Yes, I think it's very important. (1) many people preserve old traditions / quite a lot; (2) today's youth are interested in society / not very interested. / (a. ippou, b. muke ni, c. muke no, d. wake, e. tsutsu, f. ni tomonai, g. shidai, h. ni watatte, i. moto): (1) my father is a math researcher and my brother an astronomy researcher, so I also became interested in physics; (2) with the relocation of the bus stop, the timetable has also changed; (3) at this inn you can enjoy the view of Mt. Fuji while bathing in the hot spring; (4) due to the recession, stock prices keep falling; (5) these clothes are designed for young people, but they suit grandma very well too; (6) talks among the participating countries' leaders were held a total of five times; (7) as soon as the situation is confirmed, we will notify you; (8) the election was held under the observation of the election monitoring team. / Honorifics example: suru → nasaru → nasaimasu (1) say; (2) go; (3) drink; (4) be; (5) eat; (6) see; (7) give (kureru). / Humble example: kuru → mairu → mairimasu (1) go; (2) say; (3) see; (4) be; (5) ask; (6) meet; (7) do. / Necessity: you can get a job after graduating → It's not necessarily the case that you can get a job after graduating. (1) all Japanese people can use keigo correctly; (2) all women like brand-name bags; (3) in sumo, the bigger body has the advantage. / (a. kagiri, b. bakari de naku, c. ka dou ka, d. mono de wa nai): (1) you shouldn't bully younger or weaker people; (2) Nakamura has a bright personality and is kind to everyone, so she's popular; (3) as long as you're enrolled in this school, you can use its facilities; (4) before buying shoes, try them on to see if the size fits. / (a. wake ga nai, b. shidai da, c. rashii desu, d. te hajimete, e. mitai desu): (1) since I started spending time with foreign friends, I've come to want to know more about my own country; (2) it takes three hours from Kyoto, so we should arrive at 2; (3) which solution to choose depends on your way of thinking; (4) George is always positive and loves fun — very American of him; (5) look, that cloud looks like a big loaf of bread! / (a. wake de wa nai, b. hazu da, c. sae, d. mama, e. ue de, f. wake ga nai): (1) an American who only started learning Japanese last year can't possibly read classical literature full of kanji; (2) it's not that I want to attend that dinner, but I was asked, so I have to go; (3) this is a famous hotel, so the food must be delicious — looking forward to it; (4) if I don't find a job soon, I won't even be able to pay the rent; (5) you must not enter a tatami room wearing slippers; (6) in advancing the investigation, it is necessary to hear opinions from everyone involved. / (a. te kara de nai to, b. ageku, c. uchi ni, d. te hajimete, e. ue ni, f. wa mochiron): (1) the student council president has a good personality and is enthusiastic, so the council is well organized; (2) write the ingredients in your notebook so you don't forget them; (3) the town of Asakusa is lively not only on Sundays but on weekdays too; (4) when this fruit's flesh gets bigger, it's not tasty; (5) big jobs succeed only after careful preparation; (6) after much hesitation about whether to quit the company, I decided to quit after all. / (A: a. tsutsu aru, b. ni sotte, c. nara de wa, d. sae, e. ni yori, f. ni kansuru, g. nuki de, h. ni shite wa, i. mama): (1) for detailed information such as the schedule and voting, please see the homepage; (2) construction was suspended due to budget shortage, and it's unknown whether it will resume; (3) today's daytime high only reached 10 degrees, so it looks to be a cold day for late March; (4) with technological progress, people's awareness is changing; (5) how about thinking about the uniqueness that small and medium enterprises have, which big companies lack; (6) joking aside, please think more seriously; (7) customer service should be conducted according to the manual. / (B: a. kanenai, b. kanemasu, c. ue de, d. to tomo ni, e. ni yotte, f. ni atatte, g. dake atte): (1) as the sunlight strengthens and temperatures rise, flowers begin to bloom one after another; (2) after confirming the contract contents, please sign and seal here; (3) this region suffered great damage from the tsunami; (4) if you tell that guy a secret, he'll end up telling the whole class; (5) for hosting the Olympics, securing construction sites for venues is also an important issue; (6) as expected of a graduate of a prestigious school — the quality of the assigned work is high; (7) I cannot agree with actions that only consider one's own profit. / Choose the best option: (a. ni hikikae, b. o oite hoka ni nai, c. mo saru koto nagara, d. to wa ienai made mo, e. o tsuujite, f. to mo naru to): (1) having achieved 100% of the sales target, it can be called a satisfactory result; (2) I'll be 35 next year and my workplace isn't fun, so if I'm changing jobs, now is the time; (3) as the Prime Minister, every single word and action has great influence; (4) the charm of Tanaka's book, who worked as a journalist for many years, is not only the content but also the sharp, easy-to-read, interesting writing; (5) while the bride is a devoted and elegant woman, the groom is a lazy and self-centered man — truly casting pearls before swine; (6) I wondered if it was an illusion, but around noon the military's report announced over the radio that Hiroshima had been bombed. / Choose one from a-d: (1) Kyoto's landscape ordinance, established to protect its outstanding nature and historic scenery — the exterior is designed to harmonize with the traditional townscape (b. in accordance with); (2) whatever the country, a country that doesn't value its young people has no future (d. de arou to); (3) despite the lack of evidence, he continued to maintain his innocence (c. regardless of); (4) even young people indifferent to religion often go to temples or shrines at New Year (a. when it comes to); (5) the manzai duo's A's retorts are funny, while B's are crude (d. in contrast to); (6) whether this attempt succeeds depends on the residents' cooperation (c. depends on). / (a. o mochimashite, b. beku, c. ni kotaete, d. ni atte, e. ni saishi, f. o hajime to suru, g. ni todomarazu, h. atte, i. nagara): (1) please be careful of choking on foods such as hard beans and nuts; (2) I work day and night to support my family; (3) selfish as it may be, we will be temporarily closed during the above period; (4) upon starting construction, I compiled a report summarizing the progress so far; (5) my father said that while freedom is important, it must be freedom within rules; (6) our shop will close on December 31; (7) today, when nature conservation is advocated throughout Japan, the administration is struggling to justify permitting golf course construction against public opinion; (8) the trend of emphasizing academic credentials not only robs children of their childhood but also distorts society as a whole; (9) the financial education program for elementary students nationwide had 2,000 participants last year, but in response to feedback from teachers, the quota was expanded fivefold to 10,000. / Choose one from a-d: (1) the meal the criminals left unfinished was still warm — from that, it seemed they hadn't gone far (b. judging from); (2) the organization as a whole is concealing the truth (c. gurumi); (3) this company leads the communications industry and is also actively addressing climate change (d. not only ... but also); (4) rents are soaring, so I have no choice but to move (b. sasezaru o enai); (5) in American politics, Congress cannot hold the President accountable, while the President cannot dissolve Congress (a. on the other hand); (6) in ancient Egypt, preserving the body after death was valued, and mummification was widely practiced — perhaps because they feared the "second death," after which one cannot be reborn (b. perhaps for that reason); (7) no matter how harsh the circumstances, I want to avoid losing myself (c. even in).
